summary: Generalizes the use of a packet's TTL (IPv4) or Hop Limit (IPv6) to protect protocols from CPU-utilization attacks. It suits protocols such as BGP, MSDP and LDP, especially between directly connected peers. It is experimental and has been replaced by RFC 5082.

eli5.summary: If you only talk to your next-door neighbor, a shout from far away is suspicious. This trick checks a packet's travel counter to ignore messages that came from too far away. RFC 5082 replaced it.

questions: how to protect routers from remote attacks using ttl
